_comment: READING IS PUBLIC, SO THE ORIGIN LIST WAS PROTECTING NOTHING. The bucket serves these objects to anyone who has the url — that is the whole point of a public bucket, and it is how every on the site loads. Restricting GET to four named origins therefore blocked no attacker; it only blocked our own fetch() calls, which is a different code path to and is the one the studio uses to re-open a comic. That is ESK-6003: a Vercel preview deploy and localhost:3000 are separate origins from www.eski.lol, so opening an eski in the studio from either got no Access-Control-Allow-Origin back and failed. Writing is the half that needs an allowlist, and it keeps one.

Uploads. A presigned PUT is already unforgeable without the signature, but there is no reason to let any page on the internet spend one, so this half stays named. Add a preview origin here only if you need to publish from it.
